DUNGEONS OF DEATH — graphics loader and main game

The Spectrum Show source contains a 48K TZX tape with two separate BASIC programs. We kept the original TZX unchanged and the supplied TAP reconstruction. We recovered all 68 numbered lines of the graphics loader and 531 lines of the main DUNGEON program through the ZX-UX ROM listing tool. The original Dungeons.txt instructions explain the command keys and the tape loading sequence. No BASIC text was invented or rewritten.

We loaded the original TZX in Fuse 48K. At the loader's question about printing characters, we entered N. The next tape program initialized the map and displayed random player statistics. We chose C to continue, bought the first armour and weapon options, then reached the level-one map. At the command prompt, we used E, S, and W. The game showed a sinkhole at 1,5, the player reached level two, and the next view reported an empty room. The maze does not ask permission before dropping us a floor.

These views prove the game reached active text-and-map play. They do not show the magic orb being found or the quest being finished. Chance encounters can alter the exact view on a replay. The screenshots are genuine Fuse captures; no images from the source archive were passed off as gameplay.

The original Dungeons.txt lists N/S/E/W for movement, U for stairs, F for a flare, and other context actions. Only E, S and W were tested in the recorded game. bin/ is reserved for later use; no native output was created.
